# Purpose and scope

Cation exchange chromatography is Step `{python} step_no` of the A-Mab drug substance
process and is the polishing step of the purification train. This plan states how the step
will be characterized, which parameters will be varied and over what ranges, which
attributes will be measured, and by what rules the results will be judged. It is written
before the study is executed and reports no findings.

The study will be performed at the sending site on a qualified scale-down model of the
commercial column. The commercial process is operated at a production bioreactor scale of
`{python} f"{scale_l:,}"` L, and the purification train is sized to that batch. Every range
this study establishes will be derived from data generated on the scale-down model and
applied to the commercial process, so the qualification of that model is itself part of the
study and is described in §5.1.

The scope covers the `{python} n_params` operating parameters of the step listed in
@tbl-params, the `{python} n_resp` responses measured on the eluate pool, and the
`{python} n_cqa` quality attributes the step governs, which are listed in @tbl-cqa. The step
forms none of those attributes. Each of them is established upstream, and this step reduces
aggregate, host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A towards the levels the drug
substance requires. The parameter ranges to be studied are wider than the normal operating
ranges of the commercial process, so that the study bounds a knowledge space and not only the
routine operating point.

Four activities lie outside this plan. Viral clearance is claimed at the low pH
inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration steps, and no clearance claim will be made
for cation exchange, although a cation exchanger does remove virus [@amab2009]. Resin life
cycle, column packing and sanitization are controlled under SOP-2008 and are qualified in a
separate study. Validation of the analytical methods is complete and is recorded in the
method validation reports listed in @tbl-sop. Confirmation of the ranges at commercial scale
belongs to Stage 2 and will be performed during process performance qualification at the
receiving site [@fda2011].

Prior knowledge from the platform indicates that glycosylation and charge variants are not
modified across a cation exchange step operated under platform conditions [@amab2009]. Those
attributes will therefore not be measured in this study, and the plan makes no claim about
them.

# Objectives

The study has five objectives.

1. To quantify the effect of each studied parameter on the aggregate content, the host cell
   protein content and the yield of the eluate pool, over the ranges given in @tbl-params.
2. To identify the interactions between those parameters and to fit a predictive model of
   each response over the region the design covers.
3. To define the region of the multivariate space over which the governed attributes stay
   within the criteria of §7, and to establish a proven acceptable range for each parameter
   against each attribute it governs.
4. To classify every parameter of the step under SOP-4001 and to establish whether each
   normal operating range lies inside the corresponding proven acceptable range.
5. To state the contribution of the step to the control strategy, including the in-process
   controls and the parameter ranges that will be carried into process performance
   qualification.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

The step is operated in bind and elute mode on a strong cation exchange resin. Below its
isoelectric point the antibody carries a net positive charge and binds the negatively charged
ligand. Species that are acidic at the load pH do not bind and leave in the flow through. The
antibody is then eluted by raising the pH of the buffer, which weakens the electrostatic
attraction between the antibody and the ligand, and the eluate pool is collected between a
start point on the ascending edge of the elution peak and a stop point on its descending
edge.

Aggregate is retained more strongly than monomer, because a dimer presents twice the charged
surface to the ligand. It therefore elutes after the monomer, and the clearance the step
achieves depends on how well the two species are resolved and on where the pool is stopped.
Three of the studied parameters act on that resolution. Loading the column more heavily
broadens both peaks and brings the aggregate front forward into the monomer. A higher elution
buffer pH weakens the binding of both species, brings them off earlier and compresses the
separation on which the clearance depends. Collecting further into the descending edge takes
the leading part of the aggregate peak into the pool.

Most host cell proteins are acidic at the operating pH and do not bind the cation exchanger,
so the bulk of them leaves in the load flow through. The weakly bound remainder is displaced
during the wash. A higher wash conductivity shields the charge on the ligand and on the bound
species and strips more of that remainder before elution, while the antibody, which binds
more strongly, stays bound. A heavier load leaves less free ligand, and host cell protein
that the wash would otherwise have displaced co-adsorbs with the antibody. Protein load and
wash conductivity act on the same population of weakly bound species, so an interaction
between them is expected on the host cell protein content of the pool.

DNA is strongly negatively charged and is repelled by the cation exchange ligand, so it
passes through in the load. Its clearance is large and is not expected to depend on the
operating parameters. Leached Protein A and its fragments are acidic and do not bind under
the load conditions, and the fraction that is complexed with the antibody is released and
passed through when the complex binds the ligand. The clearance of leached Protein A is
therefore a property of the chemistry of the step and not of any parameter studied here.

Yield is lost at the two edges of the pool, as monomer left in the tail beyond the stop point
and as monomer that co-elutes with the aggregate that is cut away. A heavier load broadens
the peak and increases both losses. The elution stop collect point is the direct handle on
the trade between aggregate clearance and yield, and quantifying that trade is one of the
reasons the step is studied multivariately.

Prior product knowledge for this step is extensive. The same cation exchange resin and the
same platform buffer system have been used for three previously licensed humanized IgG1
antibodies, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and through the A-Mab clinical and engineering campaigns.
Across those products the step has behaved as the mechanism above predicts, and its
performance has been consistent [@amab2009]. Characterization is therefore expected to
confirm and bound relationships that are already understood. Prior knowledge is used here to
select the parameters, to set the ranges and to state the direction in which each parameter
is expected to act, and every quantitative claim in PCR-007 will rest on the data generated
under this plan.

The position of the step in the train sets what is at stake. No step downstream of cation
exchange reduces aggregate, so the aggregate content of the eluate pool carries through to
the drug substance. Host cell protein is cleared again at the anion exchange step, so the
criterion this step has to meet for host cell protein is looser than the drug substance
specification. Both criteria are derived in §8.

## Quality attributes in scope

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(CEX_CQA_KEYS))
```

: Quality attributes governed by the cation exchange step, with their acceptance criteria and criticality. {#tbl-cqa}

@tbl-cqa lists the `{python} n_cqa` attributes this step governs. Each is established
upstream of the step, and the step clears it. Criticality is assigned by the impact of the
attribute on safety and efficacy combined with the uncertainty in that impact, and attributes
of high and very high criticality are called critical [@amab2009]. Criticality is a
continuum, and an attribute of moderate criticality is controlled with the same rigour as a
critical one where the process is what sets its level [@ichq9].

Aggregate and host cell protein will be carried as responses of the designed experiments.
Both are predicted by the mechanism of §4.1 to respond to the parameters of the step, and
both are governed by this step to a degree that the criteria of §8 make demanding. Step yield
will be carried as a third response. It is a process performance attribute and not a quality
attribute, and it is measured here because it is what the aggregate criterion trades against.

Residual DNA and leached Protein A will not be carried as design responses. The mechanism
predicts that neither binds the ligand and that the clearance of both is insensitive to the
studied parameters, and the platform history supports that expectation. Both will be measured
on the eluate pool of the centre point runs and of the runs at the edges of the design, and
the results will be reported in PCR-007 as confirmatory data. Should either show a dependence
on a studied parameter, it will be treated as an unexpected result and investigated before
the operating region is defined.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters

RA-001 ranked the parameters of every unit operation before any characterization study was
designed, by the method of the case study [@amab2009] and the principles of ICH Q9 [@ichq9].
Each parameter was scored on its potential impact on a quality attribute and on its potential
to interact with other parameters. Where no data or rationale was available to support a
lower ranking, the parameter was ranked at the highest level. The scope of this plan is the
output of that assessment for the cation exchange step.

The assessment placed the parameters of the step in three groups. `{python} n_multi`
parameters were assigned to the multivariate designs, because each acts on a governed
attribute and is expected to interact with at least one other parameter.
`{python} n_uni` parameter was assigned to univariate assessment, because its effect on the
separation is expected to be small across the range the equipment permits. The remaining
operating conditions of the step, such as the buffer composition, the bed height and the
equilibration volume, are controlled to platform specification and were ranked low. They are
verified at buffer release and column release and will not be varied.

The ranges to be studied were set wider than the normal operating ranges of the commercial
process. A study that covers only the normal operating range cannot show where performance
begins to fail, and a wider range provides the process understanding needed to support
movement inside the design space later in the life cycle [@ichq8]. The ranges in @tbl-params
are the knowledge space of this study, and no claim will be made outside them.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

The study will be run on a laboratory column that models the commercial column. The model
will be designed on established principles of chromatography scaling, keeping the bed height,
the linear flow velocity, the residence time, and the load, wash and elution volumes
normalized to column volumes the same as at commercial scale. Column efficiency will be
verified by plate count and peak asymmetry before the column is used, under SOP-2008.

Qualification will follow SOP-1001. Replicate runs at the set-point conditions of
@tbl-params will be performed on the scale-down column, and their results compared with
commercial-equivalent data from the engineering and clinical campaigns. The comparison is
made on input and output attributes, which are the aggregate and host cell protein content of
the load and of the pool, the step yield, and the volume and conductivity of the eluate. The
acceptance criteria for the comparison are stated in §7.1. A model that does not meet them
will be modified and re-qualified before any characterization run is executed, and the
modification will be described in PCR-007.

The centre point runs of both designs are also runs at the set-point conditions. Their
replication serves two purposes. It gives the reproducibility of the model under repeat
operation, and it provides the pure error term against which lack of fit is tested (§5.5).
Because the centre points are executed inside the randomized run order of each design, they
also carry any drift in the column, the load or the assays across the execution period.

## Operation

Every run will be executed under SOP-2010. The column will be equilibrated in load buffer,
loaded to the protein load of the run, washed at the load and wash conductivity of the run,
and eluted with a step change to the elution buffer pH of the run. Pool collection will start
on the ascending edge of the elution peak at the platform threshold and will stop on the
descending edge at the elution stop collect setting of the run, which is expressed as optical
density on the descending edge. The column will then be stripped, cleaned and sanitized under
SOP-2008.

The load material will be the neutralized pool of the low pH viral inactivation step,
produced from A-Mab harvest at the sending site. A single load lot will be used within a
design block wherever material supply permits. The aggregate and host cell protein content of
the load will be measured for every run and carried in the data set, because both set the
level from which the step has to clear. Load composition is an input to the step and not a
parameter of it, so it is controlled and recorded and is not varied.

Buffers will be prepared to platform specification and released before use. The resin lot,
the column dimensions, the packing quality and the number of cycles on the column will be
recorded for every run. If the load available for a block differs materially in aggregate or
host cell protein content from the material used for model qualification, the difference will
be recorded as a deviation at the time it is found and its impact assessed in PCR-007.

## Analytical methods

Each response is measured by one validated method, and all of them are listed in @tbl-sop.
Aggregate will be measured as high molecular weight species by size exclusion chromatography
under AMV-3011. Host cell protein will be measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay under
AMV-3012. Residual DNA will be measured by quantitative polymerase chain reaction under
AMV-3014, and leached Protein A by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay under AMV-3016. Protein
concentration will be measured by ultraviolet absorbance, and the step yield will be
calculated from the product mass in the eluate pool and in the load.

Every sample will be tested by a validated method within its qualified range, and a result
outside that range will be reported as such and not extrapolated. The variability of each
method is established in its validation report and contributes to the residual variability of
the fitted models. The centre point replicates carry process variability and assay
variability together, which is the correct basis for the lack of fit test, because the models
are fitted to data that carry both.

## Sampling plan

Samples will be taken from the load, the flow through, the wash and the eluate pool of every
run. The eluate pool is the sample of record. It will be tested for aggregate, host cell
protein and protein concentration in every run of both designs and of the univariate
assessment. Residual DNA and leached Protein A will be tested on the eluate pool of the
centre point runs and of the runs at the edges of the design, as stated in §4.2. Flow through
and wash samples will be retained and will be tested where a pool result needs an
explanation.

The screening design includes `{python} cp_scr` centre point runs and the response surface
design includes `{python} cp_rsm`. Retained samples will be held under the storage conditions
qualified in the method validation reports until PCR-007 is approved.

## Statistical methods

The analysis will follow SOP-1002. The factors will be coded so that the set-point is 0 and
the edges of the characterization range are −1 and +1. Coding puts the estimated effects of
parameters measured in different units on a common scale, which is what makes them
comparable.

The screening design will be analysed by ordinary least squares on a model containing the
main effects and the two factor interactions. An effect will be reported as twice the coded
coefficient, which is the change in the response across the full characterization range of
the factor. Significance will be judged at α = 0.05.

The response surface design will be analysed on the full quadratic model in the same factors,
containing the main effects, the two factor interactions and the pure quadratic terms. Model
adequacy will be judged on the coefficient of determination (R²), the adjusted R², the
predicted R² computed from the prediction error sum of squares, the F test of the regression,
and the analysis of variance partition of the residual variance into lack of fit and pure
error. The pure error comes from the centre point replicates. The diagnostics reported for
each fitted response will be the residuals against the predicted values, a normal quantile
plot of the residuals, and the predicted against the actual values.

The screening model identifies which effects are active. The response surface model is the
predictive model, and it is the basis of the operating region, of the proven acceptable
ranges and of the capability estimate. A two-level design in `{python} n_scr_f` factors
cannot separate curvature from the main effects, so no predictive claim will be made from the
screening analysis.

Process capability will be estimated by Monte Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` batches, with the parameters of the step drawn inside their normal
operating ranges and the fitted response surface models used to predict each response.
Capability will be reported as a one-sided Cpk against the drug substance criterion of each
attribute, because capability states what the process delivers to the specification and not
what an intermediate pool has to meet. Every simulation will be run under a fixed random
seed, which is recorded in the analysis script, so that a reported value can be reproduced
exactly from the same data.

## Screening design

The screening study will be a two-level full factorial design in the `{python} n_scr_f`
multivariate parameters, augmented with `{python} cp_scr` centre point runs. It comprises
`{python} n_scr_fact` factorial runs and `{python} n_scr` runs in total. A full factorial
estimates all `{python} n_scr_f` main effects and all `{python} n_2fi` two factor
interactions without aliasing between them. That matters at this step, because protein load
is expected to interact with wash conductivity on host cell protein and with elution buffer
pH on aggregate, and a design that confounded either pair with a main effect could not
separate the two explanations.

The runs will be performed in randomized order, with the centre point runs distributed
through the sequence. The centre points also give a test for curvature. A difference between
the mean of the centre points and the mean of the factorial runs indicates that a two-level
model does not describe the response, which is the condition the response surface design is
there to resolve. The planned matrix is given in Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The response surface study will be a face centred central composite design in the same
`{python} n_rsm_f` parameters. It comprises `{python} n_rsm_fact` factorial runs,
`{python} n_rsm_axial` axial runs and `{python} cp_rsm` centre point runs,
`{python} n_rsm` in total. The axial runs are placed on the faces of the cube, so that no run
leaves the characterization range of any parameter and no material is produced under
conditions this plan has not bounded.

The design adds the pure quadratic terms to the model, and curvature is expected on at least
two of the responses. The aggregate content of the pool depends on where the pool is stopped
on a peak whose shape changes with load and with elution pH, and a response of that kind is
not linear across a range as wide as the one studied here. The yield is bounded above, so it
has to curve as the collected fraction is widened. The planned matrix is given in Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

`{python} flow_name` will be assessed one parameter at a time. Runs will be performed at the
lower edge, the set-point and the upper edge of its characterization range, which are
`{python} f"{flow_lo:g}"`, `{python} f"{flow_sp:g}"` and `{python} f"{flow_hi:g}"`
`{python} flow_unit`, with the multivariate parameters held at their set-points. The eluate
pools will be tested by the methods of §5.3.

The parameter was not placed in the multivariate designs because flow rate acts on resolution
through residence time, and at the particle size of the platform resin the change in
resolution across the range the equipment permits is expected to be small. The univariate
assessment tests that expectation and supports the range. Should it show an effect on
aggregate or host cell protein comparable with the effects of the multivariate parameters,
the parameter will be added to a supplementary response surface study before the operating
region is defined, and this plan will be revised.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

This section states the rules by which the study will be judged. They are fixed before
execution, and a change to any of them after approval requires a revision of this plan.

## Scale-down model qualification

The scale-down model will be accepted when the pool attributes and the step yield of the
qualification runs show no statistically significant difference from the
commercial-equivalent data at α = 0.05, and when the packed column meets the plate count and
asymmetry criteria of SOP-2008. A model that fails either test will be modified and
re-qualified, and no characterization run will be executed until it passes. The qualification
result will be reported in PCR-007 with the comparison it rests on.

## Model adequacy

A response surface model will be accepted as predictive when the regression is significant at
α = 0.05, the lack of fit is not significant against the pure error from the centre point
replicates, the predicted R² is consistent with the adjusted R², and the diagnostics show no
structure in the residuals. A model that fails the lack of fit test will be examined for an
omitted term or an influential run before any range is derived from it.

Where no factor has a significant effect on a response over the ranges studied, the step is
robust for that response across those ranges. No predictive model will be claimed in that
case. The ranges will instead be supported by the bound the executed design provides, and the
report will say so.

## Response criteria

| Response | Criterion | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `{python} D.RESP_LABEL["aggregate_out_pct"]` | at or below `{python} f"{agg_ipc[1]:g}"` % | in-process limit, derived in §8.1 |
| `{python} D.RESP_LABEL["hcp_out_ng_mg"]` | at or below `{python} f"{hcp_ipc[1]:.0f}"` ng/mg | in-process limit, derived in §8.1 |
| `{python} D.RESP_LABEL["step_yield"]` | no acceptance criterion | process performance, monitored and reported |

: Criteria the eluate pool will be judged against in the analysis. {#tbl-crit}

@tbl-crit gives the criteria the analysis will apply to the eluate pool. The criteria for
aggregate and for host cell protein are in-process limits and not the drug substance
specifications of @tbl-cqa, for the reason given in §8.1. Step yield carries no acceptance
criterion in this study. It is reported so that the cost of the aggregate criterion is
visible, and it will be controlled through the classification of the parameters that govern
it.

## Operating region and proven acceptable ranges

The operating region will be declared over the multivariate parameters as the region inside
the characterization ranges over which every governed response is predicted to meet its
criterion in @tbl-crit. Each parameter will additionally carry a proven acceptable range for
each attribute it governs, determined as described in §8.

A normal operating range that lies inside the proven acceptable range for every attribute the
parameter governs is acceptable as it stands. Where it does not, the normal operating range
will be narrowed to lie inside, or the parameter will be classified so that the residual risk
is controlled, and PCR-007 will state which was done and why. A parameter whose proven
acceptable range is narrower than its characterization range has an edge of failure inside
the region studied, and that edge will be reported in the units of the parameter.

## Parameter classification

Every parameter of the step will be classified under SOP-4001 on two questions, whether its
variation across the range studied affects a critical quality attribute, and how well it is
controlled at commercial scale. A parameter that affects a critical quality attribute and has
a low risk of moving outside the design space will be classified as a well-controlled
critical process parameter. A parameter that affects a critical quality attribute and carries
a higher risk of moving outside the design space will be classified as a critical process
parameter. A parameter that affects process performance but no quality attribute will be
classified as a key process parameter, and a parameter with no demonstrated effect on either
will be classified as a general process parameter [@amab2009].

The classification of every parameter will be stated in PCR-007 with the reason for it,
including the parameters for which no significant effect was found. A classification that
rests on the absence of an effect will be reported as resting on that, together with the
range over which the absence was demonstrated.

## Completion of the study

The study will be complete when the scale-down model is qualified, both designs and the
univariate assessment are executed and analysed, the operating region and the proven
acceptable ranges are defined, the capability is estimated and every parameter is classified.

Departures from this plan will be recorded as deviations at the time they occur and
dispositioned in PCR-007. A deviation that invalidates a design for the definition of the
operating region will require that design to be re-executed on representative material. In
that case the invalidated data will be retained and referenced, and the reported analysis
will be the re-executed one.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis)

## The acceptance basis

The criterion the analysis applies to each attribute is the criterion that applies to the
eluate pool of this step, which is not in every case the drug substance specification. The
drug substance specification for aggregate is `{python} f"{agg_ds[1]:g}"` % high molecular
weight species and for host cell protein `{python} f"{hcp_ds[1]:g}"` ng/mg (@tbl-cqa). An
intermediate pool has to be judged against a limit that still leaves the downstream steps
able to bring the batch to those specifications.

The in-process limit is carried back from the drug substance criterion through the clearance
the downstream steps deliver in the nominal train, and is then divided by an assurance
margin. The margin is what makes the limit a control rather than a break even point, because
a limit set at the undivided ceiling would leave the drug substance dependent on every
downstream step delivering its nominal clearance exactly.

No step downstream of cation exchange reduces aggregate. The ceiling for aggregate is
therefore the drug substance criterion itself, and after the assurance margin of
`{python} f"{agg_margin:g}"` the in-process limit is `{python} f"{agg_ipc[1]:g}"` %
high molecular weight species. Host cell protein is cleared again at the anion exchange step,
so its ceiling is above the drug substance criterion, and after the assurance margin of
`{python} f"{hcp_margin:g}"` the in-process limit is `{python} f"{hcp_ipc[1]:.0f}"` ng/mg.
Both limits are given in @tbl-crit and both are fixed before execution.

Residual DNA and leached Protein A will be judged against the drug substance criteria in
@tbl-cqa. They are measured as confirmatory data and are not modelled, so no proven
acceptable range will be derived for them.

## The two analyses

A proven acceptable range will be determined for each pair of a governed attribute and a
multivariate parameter, in two forms.

The first analysis holds the other parameters at their set-points and evaluates the fitted
response surface model for the parameter of interest across its characterization range, on a
grid of `{python} par_grid_sp` points. For every parameter in the multivariate designs the
set-point is the centre of the characterization range (@tbl-params), so this analysis is
performed at the centre of the design in the coded factors. The result is the range over
which the parameter alone, with the rest of the step at target, keeps the attribute within
its criterion.

The second analysis propagates normal operating range variation into the prediction. At each
of `{python} par_grid_mc` points across the characterization range of the parameter of
interest, the other parameters will be drawn `{python} f"{par_draws:,}"` times from a
distribution centred on their set-points whose spread is set by their normal operating
ranges and truncated at the characterization range, the fitted model will be evaluated at
each draw, and the residual variability of the model will be added. The parameter is
acceptable at that point when the 95 % predictive interval of the attribute stays within its
criterion. This is a robustness criterion, so the range it returns is the narrower of the two
wherever an interaction is active.

## The decision rule and the reporting

The proven acceptable range reported for a parameter is the contiguous interval containing
the set-point over which the criterion is met. Where the criterion is met across the whole
characterization range, the proven acceptable range is the characterization range, and the
report will state that no edge of failure was found inside the region studied. Where the
criterion is not met at the set-point itself under an analysis, no range will be reported for
that pair and the result will be investigated.

Each governed attribute will be reported with a plot against the parameter that governs it,
showing the predicted response across the characterization range with the acceptable region
shaded green, and with the set-point and the normal operating range marked. Both analyses
will be shown on the same figure, and the full table of ranges will be given for every pair
of an attribute and a parameter.

Two bounds apply to a proven acceptable range determined this way. It is a section through a
multivariate model taken one parameter at a time, so two ranges may not be assumed to hold
together at their edges. The multivariate statement is the operating region of §7.4, and
PCR-007 will present it as such. The fitted model also predicts mean levels, so a range
derived from the first analysis describes where the mean of the response meets the criterion
and carries no assurance about a single batch at its edge. The second analysis is what brings
the variation of the process into the range, and the capability estimate of §5.5 is what
states the assurance at the operating point.

# Data management and integrity

Data will be recorded and retained under the ALCOA+ principles. Chromatograms and run records
will be captured in the chromatography data system and analytical results in the laboratory
information management system. Both systems are validated, both record the analyst and the
time of the entry, and the audit trail of each is enabled and reviewed. Raw data will not be
transcribed by hand into the analysis.

The analysis will be performed with scripts held under version control, and the data set
analysed in PCR-007 will be the data set released by second person review. Every reported
value will be traceable to the run record and the assay result it comes from, and every
simulation will be run under a fixed random seed, so that the whole analysis can be
reproduced from the same data.

Each run record will be reviewed against this plan by a second person before the data enter
the analysis. A departure from the plan will be recorded when it is found, with what was
done, why it was done and which runs it affects. No result will be excluded from an analysis
without a documented technical reason, and any exclusion will be reported in PCR-007 with
that reason and with the effect of the exclusion on the model.

: Functions and their responsibilities for this study. {#tbl-roles}

@tbl-roles gives the functions accountable for the study. Process Development owns the plan
and the execution, and no function may change a range, a criterion or a design without a
revision of this plan approved by the same functions that approved it. The approval record is
@tbl-appr.

# Deliverables and schedule

The deliverable of this plan is PCR-007. It will report the executed study, the operating
region, the proven acceptable ranges, the estimated capability, the classification of every
parameter and the contribution of the step to the control strategy. PCR-007 rolls up into
PCMR-001, which consolidates the campaign for the receiving site.

The study will run in five phases. Qualification of the scale-down model comes first and
gates everything after it. The screening design follows, then the response surface design,
then the analysis and the report. The univariate assessment may be executed in parallel with
the response surface design, because it uses the same load material and the same methods and
its result is not needed until the parameter classification is made.

Each phase will be released by a review of the preceding phase against the criteria of §7.
No dates are fixed in this plan. The schedule is held in PTP-001 and is coordinated with the
transfer of the analytical methods to the receiving site.

# Risks and assumptions

Four risks to the study are worth stating in advance.

The first is the representativeness of the scale-down model. Every range in PCR-007 will be
derived from data generated on a laboratory column, and the claim that those ranges hold at
commercial scale rests on the qualification of §5.1. That qualification compares performance
at the set-point, and it cannot demonstrate equivalence at the edges of the ranges studied.
This is a limitation of the approach and not of its execution, and it is why the ranges are
confirmed at scale during Stage 2.

The second is the representativeness of the load. The load is the pool of the preceding step,
and its aggregate and host cell protein content vary with upstream performance. A load that
is not representative of routine material can produce an effect that is real in the data and
wrong for the process. The load will be characterized for every run, and material that is out
of trend will be treated as a deviation before the affected data are analysed.

The third is assay variability near a limit. Residual DNA is cleared to a level far below its
criterion, and a difference measured there is a difference between two results that both sit
near the lower end of the qualified range of the method. Differences of that kind will be
attributed to the assay and will not be interpreted as parameter effects.

The fourth is material supply. The study needs load material of consistent quality across
`{python} n_runs_total` design runs and the runs of the univariate assessment. Where more
than one load lot is used, the lot will be recorded in the data set and its effect examined
before the models are fitted.

Three assumptions underlie the plan. Platform behaviour observed with X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab
is assumed to transfer to A-Mab, which the mechanism of §4.1 supports and which the
qualification runs will test at the set-point. The parameters that are not studied are
assumed to be controlled to platform specification and to contribute no material variability
to the responses. The analytical methods are assumed to be validated across the range of
values the study will generate, which the method validation reports of @tbl-sop establish.

# Approvals

This plan takes effect when it has been approved by the functions listed in @tbl-appr, and no
run will be executed before that approval. A change to the design, to the ranges or to the
acceptance criteria after approval requires a revision of this plan and a new approval by the
same functions. Any departure during execution will be recorded as a deviation and
dispositioned in PCR-007.
